features.text: The patient has lower back pain that started after twisting his left side and picking something up.
The patient's back pain is located in the middle of his lower back and sometimes radiates to the left side.
The patient's back pain worsens with sudden movements to the left.
The patient does not have numbness, tingling, or weakness in his legs.
The patient does not have a history of back problems or previous injuries.
The patient is male and is in his late 30s or early 40s.
The patient has a regular office job and does not engage in physically demanding work.
The patient has not undergone any imaging studies for his back pain yet.
The patient has not had any blood tests for inflammatory markers or autoimmune panels related to his back pain.
The patient has not experienced fever, weight loss, or night pain associated with his back pain.
The patient has diabetes and checks his blood sugar at home in the mornings.
The patient's back pain is rated as a 5 or 6 out of 10 in intensity.
